title: Rudolf Blaschka 1892 — multiplex transport chronology and handoff model
research_question: How did the 1892 journey operate when people, finished glass, plant references, documents and information are treated as independent packets rather than collapsed into Rudolf's itinerary?
thesis: The Blaschka workshop worked at distance by selective decomposition and serial, partial reassembly. Transport requirements helped determine the material, documentary and representational forms in which workshop knowledge could move.

evidence_tiers.E: hypothesis or retrieval target requiring additional evidence

events.title: U.B.346–350 dispatched
actors: Ehrhorn, Emden & Mayer named through OCR-normalized context
events.state_change: 60 plant models + 329 analytical details become five numbered freight cases
guards: Exact railway departure confirmation and Bremen arrival time remain to be isolated.
OCR corrupts forwarding-firm spelling in this page; normalization rests on cleaner repeated evidence.
events.significance: The consignment's finishing delayed Rudolf's own departure, linking one production bottleneck to two later mobility regimes.

events.title: Rudolf enters Bremen passenger system
events.state_change: workshop member becomes ticketed first-class passenger while the same commercial intermediary also belongs to the freight network
guards: Keep passenger service distinct from cargo forwarding even though the intermediary overlaps.

events.title: Cargo and passenger clocks converge at New York
events.state_change: earlier-departing cargo and later-departing traveller reach the same port at nearly the same time
guards: Rudolf says same day, cargo morning/person evening; a secondary passenger-list index gives Elbe 12 Feb and Saale 13 Feb. Preserve discrepancy until contemporary vessel records are isolated.

events.title: Rudolf passes passenger customs
events.state_change: traveller and carried articles become admitted passenger/baggage after declaration; traveller then becomes Harvard guest/research worker
guards: Do not use this event as evidence for the cargo cases' bonded procedure.

events.title: Shipping advice and papers transferred to E. A. Snow
events.state_change: arrival advice/papers become operational clearance documents before physical cases reach the museum
guards: Exact document types are not specified in the letter.
Snow's exact 1892 business identity remains a directory/customs-record retrieval target.

events.title: Cambridge seeds sent east
actors: Leopold Blaschka/Cambridge Botanic Garden as source context
events.state_change: about 29 seed species become a coded packet described by Rudolf as 'sample without value'
guards: The phrase is compatible with contemporary merchandise-sample language but does not prove a particular postal tariff/category without wrapper or receipt.

events.title: Five model boxes reach Harvard and preliminary opening begins
events.action: internal transport / outer unpacking / preliminary opening
events.state_change: freight boxes move by elevator to museum floor; outer packing and one case are opened; Datura arborea is inspected; remaining opening waits for customs authority
guards: Descriptive project prose identifies the actor as an unnamed Black museum porter/houseboy while preserving the historical source wording only when quotation is necessary.
This is preliminary opening, not the 23 Feb official inspection.

events.title: Capt. Wales performs customs inspection at museum
actors: Capt. Wales of the Custom House
events.state_change: about eight specimens are opened under customs inspection and reported in excellent condition; remaining unpacking is staged
guards: Do not infer that every item in U.B.346–350 was personally opened by Wales.

events.title: Rudolf leaves for Jamaica while Harvard receiving continues
events.state_change: traveller leaves the receiving site while the object-clearance/unpacking process remains active
guards: Exact vessel naming in OCR should be image-checked before publication.

events.title: Field organisms are decomposed into multiple reference forms
events.state_change: living plants become drawings, microscopic records, alcohol specimens, herbarium material, seeds, bulbs, cacti, or future-supply relations
guards: Each species/packet requires its own source before being mapped as a specific route.

events.title: Rudolf repairs older Harvard models
events.state_change: damaged museum models become repaired objects; some petals are newly made at Harvard with local apparatus; two severe examples are planned for return to Germany
guards: Goodale says the two badly broken examples came in the 'first consignment' and were damaged in New York customs; do not assign them to U.B.346–350.

events.title: Return is partial rather than total reassembly
events.state_change: Rudolf returns to Germany but more than 300 herbarium specimens from the 1892/1895 expeditions remain in Harvard's herbarium; other reference packets move separately
guards: Harvard finding aid combines 1892 and 1895 in the >300 total; specimen-level crosswalk is required before assigning individual sheets to one expedition.

events.title: Reference books and lagging materials continue east
events.state_change: reference literature and preserved material reach the workshop on clocks independent of Rudolf's body
guards: Resolve exact dispatch dates/contents packet by packet before public route drawing.

events.title: American reference becomes finished glass returned west
events.state_change: selected American plant references are reconstituted as glass models and shipped to Harvard
evidence: 1893 correspondence and later Ware shipment records
guards: Do not imply that every expedition specimen/reference had a one-to-one model outcome.

longitudinal_controls.finding: Harvard finding aid and workshop material place breakage in the earliest botanical-model customs encounter; later June 1892 repairs plausibly include early damage.
longitudinal_controls.guard: No direct causal document yet proves that this damage caused the later museum-side customs-opening procedure.

longitudinal_controls.finding: shipper-note error → Bristol mislanding → about two-week delay → breakage of nos.239/356 → replacements inserted into later Haddon shipment
longitudinal_controls.value: documentary error changes physical route and pushes repair across customer/order boundaries

longitudinal_controls.finding: outer package reportedly sound while six objects inside damaged; workshop suspects unpacking
longitudinal_controls.value: arrival condition cannot by itself locate the stage of damage

longitudinal_controls.finding: T.D. Downing & Co., Customs & Forwarding Agents, bills clearance/cartage for six packages of Glass Flowers
longitudinal_controls.value: later receiving chain exposes broker and government-teamster layers

longitudinal_controls.finding: R.B.1–4 route Dresden→Bremen→New York→in bond Boston→E.A. Snow/customs broker→Harvard, while Snow's disappearance/status change later delays delivery
longitudinal_controls.value: intermediary continuity is an operational dependency and can fail

longitudinal_controls.finding: cheaper direct-Boston route rejected because new consular documentation and delay would be required; established New York-in-bond route retained
longitudinal_controls.value: documentary architecture creates route path dependence

longitudinal_controls.finding: packing material protects glass but alarms customs/quarantine official; slight breaks repaired by Bierweiler
longitudinal_controls.value: one material can reduce mechanical risk and increase regulatory risk

longitudinal_controls.finding: cardboard plate/box+tissue+wood/straw/burlap transit architecture; customs opening in museum; model removed from transit support and remounted on gypsum plaque
longitudinal_controls.value: transport creates an engineered intermediate object state

longitudinal_controls.finding: Rudolf explicitly credits Bierweiler's skill/care in unpacking complicated models after highly successful arrival
longitudinal_controls.value: receiving-side tacit skill is part of the transport system

longitudinal_controls.finding: living marine animals move Trieste→workshop while glass models move opposite direction; transportability depends on robustness, temperature and packing; routing dispute affects supply relationship
longitudinal_controls.value: counterflow and transport selection alter epistemic access

known_data_model_gaps.finding: Both 1892 CSVs have zero occurrences of Elbe, Snow, Wales, bond, freight, custom, Bremen, 346, Datura, Saale and Ehrhorn, despite direct archive evidence for them.

known_data_model_gaps.finding: Harvard official finding aid says >300 1892/1895 expedition herbarium specimens remained at Harvard.
known_data_model_gaps.implication: return-to-Hosterwitz lines require specimen-level selection/duplication evidence
